Maria Nguyen: Hey folks — planning to bring up a 12-node GPU cluster in Azure (eastus2) for a new training fleet. Need help with VNet/subnet sizing, outbound scaling (SNAT), and peering to shared-services.

Maria Nguyen: Current plan: /20 VNet, two /24 subnets (ingest + compute). Will attach VM scale sets with Standard_ND96asr_v4. We expect ~5k concurrent outbound connections, lots of short-lived egress to artifact storage.

Kai Patel: /24 for compute should be fine for IPs, but watch the SNAT port exhaustion per NAT gateway IP. If you're hitting >64k ephemeral ports we need multiple public IPs on the NAT gateway.

SRE Lead: +1. Also need subscription ID, resource group, and whether peering to shared-services requires gateway transit (we can't use transitive peering without hub/spoke config).

Maria Nguyen: Sub: redwood-infra-prod, RG: rg-gpu-eastus2. Yes we'd like peering to shared-services (hub) for logging/metrics + Key Vault PrivateLink. Can we do a hub-and-spoke with a managed NAT in the hub?

Ashley Romero: Hub NAT is ok, but note cost and single point of egress. For scale and isolation we usually colocate NAT gateway per spoke and add extra public IPs. Also consider Service Tags + PrivateLink for storage to reduce egress.

Kai Patel: Quick checks — run these and paste outputs:
```
az vm list-usage --location eastus2 --output table
az network public-ip list --query "[].{name:name,sku:sku,ipAddress:ipAddress}"
az network nat gateway show -g rg-gpu-eastus2 -n nat-gpu --query "{ips:publicIpAddresses}" -o json
```

SRE Lead: I'll open a Microsoft quota ticket for VM/accelerator quota and SNAT if you want. We'll need: region, SKU (Standard_ND96asr_v4), desired cores (e.g., 12 nodes x 96 vCPUs = 1152), and justification (training cluster for model infra).

Maria Nguyen: Thanks — posting numbers here: 12 nodes, each node 96 vCPUs, 12 GPUs total (ND96). Requesting quota bump to 1500 vCPUs and GPU SKU increase for ND-series to cover expansion. Also need NAT SNAT capacity increased: estimate 200k concurrent ephemeral ports.

Devops Bot: Support request created with Microsoft -> SR# 2203345678. Status: Pending. Link: https://portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_Azure_Support/HelpAndSupportBlade/~/supportRequestId/2203345678 :ticket: 

Cloud Ops: FYI — NAT gateway scales by adding public IPs. Each Standard Public IP gives ~64k ports. For 200k ports you'd need 4 public IPs (64k*4 > 200k). Each additional IP is ~$X/month — factor into cost.

Ashley Romero: For PrivateLink to Key Vault/storage: create Private Endpoint in the spoke and approve from hub subscription (if cross-sub). May need RBAC + DNS zone (privatelink.blob.core.windows.net) delegation.

Kai Patel: On peering: ensure "use remote gateways" or "allow gateway transit" settings are set correctly. If hub firewall is doing egress, allow forwarded traffic. Example command to create peering: 
```
az network vnet peering create --name spoke-to-hub --resource-group rg-gpu-eastus2 --vnet-name vnet-spoke --remote-vnet /subscriptions/<hub-sub>/resourceGroups/rg-hub/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/vnet-hub --allow-vnet-access --allow-gateway-transit
```

Maria Nguyen: Perfect. One ask from security: can we avoid public outbound by routing storage traffic to PrivateLink entirely? That'd reduce SNAT needs.

SRE Lead: Yes for blob/kv — PrivateLink is best. For external APIs we'll still need egress. Consider using an egress proxy in hub with egress filtering to reduce SNAT footprint.

Maria Nguyen: I'll update the ticket SR#2203345678 with PrivateLink plan and the vCPU/GPU quota numbers. Thanks for the quick help.

Kai Patel: I'll follow up on the peering change and create a short runbook for hub/spoke NAT IP sizing and DNS delegation.

Ashley Romero: Noted — I'll validate cost estimate and share with finance.

Devops Bot: SR#2203345678 updated by SRE Lead. Status: Awaiting MS approval. :hourglass:
